name: browser-app-builder
description: Guide a student from local setup to a planned, tested browser app and GitHub Pages publication, with bundled Campus Designer styling.

interface.shortDescription: Plan, build, evaluate, and publish a browser app. No coding experience is required.
interface.longDescription: Turn a problem you understand into a self-contained browser application, with a saved plan, local revision history, calculation evidence, and a GitHub Pages publishing workflow. Your agent handles the files and commands; you make the product and model decisions. Includes five workflow skills, a minimal starter, a Pages workflow, and the bundled Campus Designer branding skill. Build explicitly uses Campus Designer's Duke colors, typography, web, and review guidance. Explore three live examples below, built in automated trials with simulated student conversations and synthetic data.
defaultPrompt: Use setup-browser-app to prepare this folder.
Use plan-browser-app to help me plan a pricing scenario calculator.
Use build-browser-app to implement the agreed PLAN.md.
Use evaluate-browser-app to check the calculations with me and record the evidence.
Use deploy-browser-app to help me publish the evaluated app on GitHub Pages.

io.github.jordanmeyer.label: Pilot candidate · Instructor-built
io.github.jordanmeyer.audience: MBA students building a self-contained decision tool, dashboard, or simulation with an agent.

results.label: Automated app trials published and verified live
Passing pricing cases / inventory test groups / sales cases
Updated apps verified after cache corrections

io.github.jordanmeyer.method: On October 8, 2026, three parallel agents used version 0.1.1 to build original apps from blank folders on a configured Mac. Simulated planning conversations, independent expected results, browser checks, source repositories, and live Pages deployments are recorded. Browser tests passed 25 pricing cases, 10 inventory groups, and 42 sales cases. Testing caught and corrected two reset bugs; live update checks caught stale JavaScript in all three apps, corrected in a third deployment per repository. The coordinator handled shared browser operations. These are automated trials, not real student outcomes or ChatGPT Work trials.
io.github.jordanmeyer.limits: Apps run in the browser using public/synthetic datasets or locally selected files. No backends, logins, external APIs, remote AI, analytics, or secret keys. The host must provide usable file, Git, preview, and browser capabilities. This is a pilot candidate; Work, clean-machine, fresh-chat, and novice-student checks remain outstanding. Live publication and updates were verified on this configured Mac. Evaluation supports specific claims about tested cases; it does not certify a business model.
